docs.summary: The project-wide agent type table (mirrors [`NavMeshAreas`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAreas)): defined in the editor's navigation settings, restored in players from Navigation.yaml, with a code-side default (the built-in Humanoid, id 0) so headless and procedural use needs no settings file.
The built-in default agent type id. Always present; cannot be removed.
All defined agent types, in table order. Do not mutate the entries — use [`ApplyTable`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgentTypes~ApplyTable) (settings) to change the table.
The agent type with the given id, or null when undefined.
Display name for an agent type id ("Agent Type N" for undefined ids, so stale references stay visible rather than blank).
Replace the table (called by settings loading). The built-in Humanoid entry is enforced: id 0 always exists and keeps its name, though its envelope values are editable.

members.name: GetBuildSettings
members.signature: public static NavMeshBuildSettings GetBuildSettings(int agentTypeId, NavMeshBuildOverrides? overrides = null)

docs.summary: Compose the resolved bake input for an agent type: envelope from the table, everything else from `overrides` (or defaults). This is what surfaces hand to [`Build`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshBuilder~Build); the builder API itself only ever sees the resolved [`NavMeshBuildSettings`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshBuildSettings). An undefined id falls back to the Humanoid envelope with a warning — a bake with wrong-but-sane dimensions beats no bake.
